h34s lets you write Nuxt/Nitro server routes in Scala.js. In this release, Kyo is the core: one runtime owns the request lifecycle, cancellation, streaming, error rendering, runtime configuration and application-scoped resources. ZIO applications use a hand-written, first-class adapter over that core. Kyo applications never depend on ZIO; ZIO applications get Kyo through the adapter. Your application owns its models, services, configuration and the optional `AppHandler` that wires them.

This is a breaking alpha. Handlers, the module set and the wire format changed; see [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes) before you upgrade from `0.1.0-alpha.1`.

These notes are attached to the GitHub prerelease only after the release workflow publishes the artifacts and verifies authenticated consumers against GitHub Packages.

## Install

Artifacts use organization **`dev.yuri4n`**, version **`0.2.0-alpha.1`**, and the private Maven registry at `https://maven.pkg.github.com/yuri4n/h34s`. Use sbt's `%%%` operator for the `_sjs1_3` coordinates. Build with **Scala 3.9.0** and **Java 25**.

Follow the [installation and authentication guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/v0.2.0-alpha.1/docs/releases.md). Downloads require repository access and a classic GitHub token with `read:packages`. The h34s repository's own workflows use their `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Other repositories, including `yurian.land`, must supply a classic PAT through Actions secrets, because Maven packages use repository-scoped permissions. Save the secret as `PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN` and the username variable as `PACKAGES_USER`, then map them into the process environment variables `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_PACKAGES_USER`. GitHub reserves the `GITHUB_` prefix for saved secret and variable names.

```scala
// Kyo application
libraryDependencies += "dev.yuri4n" %%% "kyo-h3-ext" % "0.2.0-alpha.1"

// ZIO application
libraryDependencies += "dev.yuri4n" %%% "zio-h3-ext" % "0.2.0-alpha.1"
```

In the Nuxt application, also install:

- **`@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt@0.2.0-alpha.1`** as a dev dependency, from the private npm registry (`@yuri4n:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`). It has its own [npm release](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/releases/tag/npm-v0.2.0-alpha.1), which is published before this one. These libraries need its new Nitro plugin. With `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt@0.1.0-alpha.1`, `RuntimeConfig`, `KHubKv.mount` and their ZIO versions fail with `ConfigError("h34s Nitro plugin is not installed")`.
- **`h3@1.15.4`** as a runtime dependency.

| Artifact | Purpose | Brings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `h3-ext` | Native layer: the `Request` snapshot, `ResponseHead`, `HandlerOptions`, `SafeError`, `HttpError`, `InvalidInput`, `Secret`; internal h3, Node and Nitro facades | No effect runtime |
| `kyo-h3-ext` | The core: `KHandler`, `Response`, body reading, `RuntimeConfig`, `Shared`, streaming | Kyo |
| `kyo-nuxthub-ext` | Optional Kyo storage over Nitro mounts (`KHubKv.mount`) | Kyo |
| `native-converter-kyo-schema-ext` | Optional `derives NativeSchema` from a Kyo `Schema` | Kyo Schema |
| `zio-h3-ext` | The ZIO adapter: `ZHandler`, ZIO `Response`, `ZRuntimeConfig`, `ZShared`, `ZStream` bodies | ZIO and Kyo |
| `zio-nuxthub-ext` | Optional ZIO storage over Nitro mounts (`ZHubKv.mount`) | ZIO and Kyo |
| `native-converter-zio-ext` | NativeConverter instances for ZIO data types | ZIO, no Kyo |
| `native-converter-zio-json-ext` | NativeConverter instances for ZIO JSON values | ZIO JSON, no Kyo |
| `native-converter-zio-schema-ext` | Optional `derives NativeSchema` from a ZIO `Schema` | ZIO Schema, no Kyo |

Schema support stays optional: plain `derives NativeConverter` models need neither schema bridge. The bridges do not choose a JSON or YAML library for you. Add `kyo-schema-json`, `kyo-schema-yaml` or `zio-schema-json` yourself when you need those formats, and add `"dev.zio" %%% "zio-schema-derivation" % "1.7.5"` with the ZIO Schema bridge. Applications, examples, aggregates and the experimental migration module are not published.

## Features and behavior

- **Handlers are functions.** A handler takes an immutable `Request` snapshot and returns the body: `KHandler.define(request => ...)` or `ZHandler.define(request => ...)`. Status, headers and cookies are local state (`Var[ResponseHead]` in Kyo, `ZState[ResponseHead]` in ZIO) that you change with `Response.status`, `Response.header` and `Response.cookie`. h34s writes the head once, after your program and its finalizers finish. Normal handler code needs no `js.native`, `js.Promise`, facades or TypeScript glue.
- **Bounded request bodies.** `request.body.json[A]` and `request.body.text()` read at most 1 MiB by default. A non-JSON content type answers 415, a body above the limit 413, invalid JSON 400, and a body that the converter or schema rejects 422.
- **Wire format.** With the default options, a value is `{"data": ...}`, `Unit` is 204 without a body, and an error is `{"errors": [{"message": "...", "path": "..."}]}`. `HandlerOptions` selects raw success bodies (`SuccessEnvelope.Raw`), a single `{"error": ...}` entry (`ErrorEnvelope.SingleOrList`), response defaults, the body limit and a strict JSON content type.
- **Safe errors and diagnostics.** A `SafeError` is public: its status, entries and headers reach the client. Any other `Throwable`, panic or ZIO defect answers an opaque 500 with `Internal server error`. On a failure, only response defaults, entries marked `OnFailure.Keep` and the error's own headers stay in the response. The entry carries `debug.cause` (the exception chain in Kyo, `Cause.prettyPrint` in ZIO) only in Nuxt development or when `runtimeConfig.h34s.debug` is true, for example with `NUXT_H34S_DEBUG=true`. A request cannot turn diagnostics on. Keep debug mode off in production.
- **Client disconnects.** A disconnect interrupts Kyo and ZIO handlers. h34s waits for their finalizers, including asynchronous ZIO finalizers and Kyo's structured child fibers, before the request settles, and then writes nothing. Interruption can roll back an open transaction instead of committing it. Wrap a step that must finish in `KHandler.uninterruptible(step)` (Kyo) or `step.uninterruptible` (ZIO).
- **Runtime config and secrets.** `RuntimeConfig` and `ZRuntimeConfig` decode Nuxt runtime config into your own models, so `NUXT_*` environment variables can override the keys you declare, at runtime. `Secret` prints as `Secret(<redacted>)`, compares a candidate in constant time for its length with `matches`, and returns the plain value only through `reveal`.
- **Application-scoped resources.** `Shared` and `ZShared` acquire a resource once, such as a database pool, share it across requests and release it when Nitro closes. Concurrent first requests share one acquisition, and a failed acquisition is not cached.
- **Streaming.** Return a `kyo.Stream[String, S]` or a `ZStream[Any, E, String]` as the body. Delivery is pull-driven, and the head is written before the first chunk. A stream without a content type is sent as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. A disconnect interrupts the producer and waits for its cleanup.
- **One schema per model.** `derives Schema, NativeSchema` gives native conversion and validation from one Kyo Schema or ZIO Schema. Failed checks answer 422 with one entry per problem and its `path`; a wrong shape answers one generic 422 entry. JSON, and YAML for Kyo, come from the same schema through the format library you add.
- **Nitro storage.** `KHubKv.mount("cache")` and `ZHubKv.mount("cache")` open a Nitro storage mount by name, with `get`, `set` (with an optional TTL), `has`, `delete` and `keys`. A stored value that does not decode fails with `StoredValueError`, which names only the failing path, never the key or the value.
- **Nitro plugin.** The `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt` module registers `runtime/h34s.mjs`. It hands the development and debug flags, runtime config, storage and a close hook to Scala, and the module declares `runtimeConfig.h34s.debug: false`. Development loads linked Scala.js modules directly, and Scala.js source maps locate Scala sources in Node stack traces. `h34s-scala build` clears previous output before it production-links, so a failed link cannot package stale development code.

## Breaking changes

`0.2.0-alpha.1` is not source-compatible with `0.1.0-alpha.1`. The [migration guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/v0.2.0-alpha.1/docs/migration.md) lists every removed or renamed API with its replacement. The main changes:

- **Toolchain:** every module builds with Scala 3.9.0 and Java 25. ZIO moves to 2.1.26, the version that kyo-zio pins.
- **Modules:** `zio-js-ext`, `nuxthub-ext` and `zio-h3-schema-ext` are removed, and `native-converter-kyo-schema-ext` is new. `zio-h3-ext` now depends on `kyo-h3-ext`, so ZIO applications resolve Kyo. `h3-ext` no longer exposes the ScalablyTyped-generated `dev.yuri4n.h34s.facades.*` packages.
- **Handlers:** `KHandler.define(program)` and `ZHandler.define(program)` become `define(request => program)`. `KH3Event`, `SH3Event` and `getEvent` are removed; use the `Request` argument. `readBody[A]` and `readBodyWithSchema[A]` become `request.body.json[A]`, `setResponseStatus` becomes `Response.status`, and `sendStream` becomes a returned stream of strings.
- **Storage:** `KHubKv(native)` and `ZHubKv(native)` become `KHubKv.mount(base)` and `ZHubKv.mount(base)`.
- **Wire format:** values are wrapped in `{"data": ...}`, error entries are objects (`{"errors": [{"message": "..."}]}`), and `Unit` answers 204. Update your TypeScript types and `fetch` code, or pass `HandlerOptions(success = SuccessEnvelope.Raw)` to keep raw success bodies.
- **Errors:** `ErrorResponse` gains a `status` field, so a one-field pattern match needs `_`. ZIO handlers use the shared `SafeError`, which has no `maybeUnderlying`.
- **npm tooling:** use `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt@0.2.0-alpha.1` with these libraries. Its Nitro plugin is now `runtime/h34s.mjs`; `runtime/development.mjs` re-exports it for one release.

Do not mix `0.1.0-alpha.1` and `0.2.0-alpha.1` modules in one application. To stay on the old API, keep every h34s dependency and `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt` at `0.1.0-alpha.1`.

## Toolchain and release checks

Use **Scala 3.9.0**, **Scala.js 1.22.0**, **Java 25**, **sbt 1.11.7**, **Node 24** and **pnpm 10.34.4**. The Kyo modules use **Kyo 1.0.0-RC7**, whose macros need Java 25 at build time. The ZIO modules use **ZIO 2.1.26**, zio-json 0.7.44 and zio-schema 1.7.5. NativeConverter is 0.9.0. Java and sbt are build tools; your application runs in Nitro on Node.

Release gates run the native, Kyo, ZIO, schema, storage and example test suites, production linking, and POM validation. The POM check fails when a Kyo artifact depends on ZIO, `h3-ext` depends on any effect runtime, a ZIO converter depends on Kyo, or a module other than a schema bridge depends on a schema library. Four independent Maven consumers (Kyo, ZIO, Kyo Schema and ZIO Schema) then compile, link and serve real h3 requests through a preemptive router, as Nitro does. They check `{"data": ...}` bodies, opaque 500s without diagnostics, 422 entries with paths and 400 for invalid JSON, and the Kyo consumers must not resolve any `dev.zio` artifact. The workflow repeats the consumer checks against the private registry before it creates this prerelease.

The npm package has its own release workflow: package tests on Node 22.18.0 and 24, Nuxt 4.3.1 development and production HTTP checks with the packed module, and an authenticated registry download that must match the tested archive before an offline install verifies it.

## Alpha limits

- **No database ran in h34s's own checks.** The ZIO demo's Skunk Notes flow and the code in the [database guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/v0.2.0-alpha.1/docs/database.md) compile, and the Notes handlers are unit-tested, but neither has run against PostgreSQL in this repository. Separately, the downstream `yurian.land` application ran its own kyo-sql code against PostgreSQL 16 in a Nitro production build, using a locally published snapshot of this source. That is evidence for one application, not a general guarantee.
- **kyo-net in Nitro bundles** is verified only by that application, where kyo-net selected its Node backend. Other bundles, Nitro presets and deployment targets are untested.
- **Scaladoc jars are omitted.** Binary and source jars are published. Use the [guides](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/tree/v0.2.0-alpha.1/docs) and the source jars.
- **Route files are still manual.** Mount each exported handler with a one-line route file, such as `export { default } from '../.scala/hello-get.js'`. Route registration is not generated yet.
- **No generated TypeScript types yet.** Write the wire types for `{"data": ...}` and `{"errors": [...]}` in your client code.
- **Build memory.** The repository example links a Kyo and a ZIO application, and its `nuxt build` needed `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`. The cause is not identified yet. A single-runtime application links less code, but check your own build.
- **h3 internals.** Disconnect handling sets h3's private `_handled` field, so that h3 does not send a fallback 404 for a response that h34s ended. It is tested with h3 1.15.4; keep h3 pinned to that version.
- **No ZIO YAML on Scala.js.** zio-json-yaml has no Scala.js artifact, so ZIO models have no YAML codec in Nitro. Kyo models get YAML from kyo-schema-yaml.
- **Stream bodies are strings.** Encode each element yourself, for example `stream.map(_.toJson + "\n")`. Streaming needs a Node HTTP response. A stream over Nitro's in-process local fetch (for example a server-side `$fetch` to your own route) is rejected with an opaque 500, and other Nitro presets are untested.
- **Other known gaps.** The ZIO Schema bridge does not support enums, sealed traits or maps yet. Kyo finalizer failures are logged and do not change the response. NuxtHub KV as a Nitro storage mount is not verified; the storage tests use Unstorage 1.17.3's memory driver. Nix/NixOS, sbt-native-packager and application packaging remain separate work. See the [compatibility matrix](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/v0.2.0-alpha.1/docs/compatibility.md) for what was verified locally, in CI and not at all.
